messages:
Kevin: Quick question — how should our cost dashboard attribute cache savings when routing falls back to a cheaper variant? e.g., request hits model-A (primary, expensive), misses cache, then routed to model-B due to SLA/capacity and returns cached prefix. Do we credit the route that originated the request or the model that served tokens? :thinking:
Nina: IMO we need both views. For chargeback you want "origin route" attribution; for infra ops you want "serving model" attribution. Otherwise teams will optimize the wrong thing.
Sam: This is the tricky part: cache savings are not additive when fallback changes token counts. If model-B returns more tokens, you might inflate savings. We should normalize by "tokens saved on serving model" vs "tokens that would have been served by primary".
Ida: We could add a toggle in the console: "Credit cache savings to: Origin route | Serving model". Default to origin route for billing. Also add a note for canaries.
Kevin: Agree on toggle. Also need to handle quotas — if a tenant hits per-route quota and we redirect to shared pool, cost should be visible but exempt from tenant bill. Anyone opposed to a flag "externalized_cost" on routed requests?
Nina: Sounds good. Implementation note: we already tag trace spans with route_id and model_variant. We need an extra enum: fallback_reason = {none, capacity, quota, version_mismatch} so dashboard logic can decide.
Sam: Pseudo SQL for amortized crediting I sketched:
```
SELECT route_id,
 SUM(CASE WHEN serving_model = primary_model THEN tokens_cost ELSE 0 END) AS primary_cost,
 SUM(CASE WHEN serving_model != primary_model THEN tokens_cost ELSE 0 END) AS fallback_cost,
 SUM(cache_saved_tokens) AS cache_savings
FROM request_events
WHERE ts BETWEEN $start AND $end
GROUP BY route_id
```
We can extend with fallback_reason and externalized_cost flags.
Ida: UX question: show a single-line hint when the toggle is on: "Includes fallbacks — costs may reflect cross-tenant routing". PMs want simplicity. Also add a tooltip for "amortized cache credits" explaining the math.
Kevin: Ops ask — we need a drilldown that shows per-request example for top 20 outliers so on-call can see why a route shows negative unit cost.
costbot: new-metric-canary created for "route_amortized_cache_credit_v1" on staging. Dashboard link: https://redwood.internal/dash/canary/123
Nina: I'll add the fallback_reason enum to the event schema. Sam — can you add the SQL and an example visualization in the prototype?
Sam: On it. I'll push a PR with query + sample viz. ETA EOD.
Kevin: Thanks — once PR lands we can run sampling job and add the console toggle behind a feature flag. :thumbsup:
